{{nihongo|'''Amamikoso Shrine'''|阿麻美許曾神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Yata|Q80932676|qid=Q80932676|lt=Yata}}, {{ill|Higashisumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|Q861264|qid=Q861264}}, {{ill|Osaka|Q35765|qid=Q35765}}. It is a shikinaisha of {{ill|Tajihinokōri district|Q11368538|qid=Q11368538}} in {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Amamikoso Shrine'''|阿麻美許曾神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}
* {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611}}

At present, the enshrined deities are the three listed above; however, the “Kongōji-bon” records only one seat, making the original principal deity unclear. Because this area was under the control of the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|Q1198447|qid=Q1198447}}, it has been conjectured—considering that “Koso” (こそ) in the shrine’s name may denote an honorific—that the Nakatomi clan’s Amanohiko-no-Mikoto was the original principal deity. On the other hand, according to the {{ill|Kujiki|Q2716751|qid=Q2716751}}, {{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836}}’s Hikomisone-no-Mikoto was appointed as the provincial ruler of Kawachi and was “buried at Amami Hill in Tanbi.” From this, another theory suggests that Hikomisone-no-Mikoto was originally enshrined here, and that after the Mononobe clan’s downfall, the Nakatomi clan occupied the area and replaced the enshrined deity <ref name = "Higashisumiyoshi explanation">{{Cite web|Japanese book| url = https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/higashisumiyoshi/page/0000032765.html | title = Osaka City Higashisumiyoshi Ward 003 Amamikoso Shrine | date = 2013-07-04 | publisher = {{ill|Osaka|Q35765|qid=Q35765}}{{ill|Higashisumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|Q861264|qid=Q861264}} | accessdate = 2015-09-13}}</ref>.

== History ==
Amamikoso Shrine is a shikinaisha, and according to shrine tradition, it was founded during the Daidō era (around Daidō 1 = 806), though it is believed to be older. “Koso” is said to derive from a word in {{ill|Silla|ar|مملكة شلا|ast|Silla (Corea)|az|Şila krallığı|azb|شیلا|bar|Silla|be|Сіла (дзяржава)|bg|Сила (държава)|bs|Kraljevstvo Sila|ca|Silla (Corea)|cdo|Sĭng-lò̤|ckb|شیللا|cs|Silla|da|Silla (koreansk stat)|de|Silla|eo|Silla|es|Silla (Corea)|eu|Silla (Korea)|fa|پادشاهی شیلا|fi|Silla|fr|Silla (Corée)|gl|Reino de Silla|hi|सिल्ला|hr|Kraljevstvo Sila|hu|Silla (ókori királyság)|id|Silla|it|Silla (Corea)|ja|新羅|ka|სილა|kk|Силла|km|ស៊ីលឡា|ko|신라|ks|سِللا سَلطَنَت|ku|Keyaniya Sillayê|lt|Šila (Korėja)|lv|Silla|mk|Сила (држава)|ml|സില്ല|mn|Шилла|ms|Silla|my|ရှီလာ|mzn|سیلا|nds|Silla|nl|Silla (Korea)|no|Silla|oc|Silla (reialme)|pl|Silla|pt|Silla (Coreia)|ro|Silla|ru|Силла|sco|Silla|sh|Sila (kraljevina)|si|සිල්ලා|simple|Silla|sk|Silla|sr|Сила (краљевство)|sv|Silla|sw|Silla|th|ชิลลา|tl|Silla|tr|Silla|uk|Сілла|vi|Tân La|wuu|新罗|zh|新罗|zh_classical|新羅|zh_min_nan|Sin-lô|zh_yue|新羅|qid=Q28456}}, and it is thought that immigrants from the {{ill|Korean Peninsula|Q483134|qid=Q483134}} may have begun the shrine by worshipping their ancestors <ref name = "Matsubara City explanation">{{Cite web|Japanese book| url = http://www.city.matsubara.osaka.jp/10,113,51,258.html | title = History Walk: 18 Amamikoso Shrine and Immigrants | date = 2009-01-09 | publisher = {{ill|Matsubara|Q774952|qid=Q774952}} | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20130704105411/http://www.city.matsubara.osaka.jp/10,113,51,258.html | archivedate = 2013-07-04 | accessdate = 2015-09-13}}</ref>.

To the east of the purification pavilion stands a stone monument inscribed “Place where Gyōki Bosatsu resided,” and there is a tradition that {{ill|Gyōki|Q1136664|qid=Q1136664}} lived here. However, this tradition appears only from around the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} <ref name = "Matsubara City explanation" />, and since no such record appears in the “Gyōki Chronology,” it is considered difficult to substantiate <ref name = "Higashisumiyoshi explanation" />.

The area including this shrine was originally part of Yata Village (later becoming part of Osaka City). During the Edo period, the rerouting of the {{ill|Yamato River|Q9001527|qid=Q9001527}} split Yata Village, leaving the shrine separated on the river’s south bank. At that time, most of the southern part of Yata Village was incorporated into what later became Matsubara City, but because the shrine was the tutelary shrine of Yata Village, only the area around the shrine and its approach remained part of Yata Village. As a result, although the shrine lies on the south bank of the Yamato River, it belongs to Osaka City, and the section corresponding to the approach (the {{ill|Kōya Kaidō|Q11673149|qid=Q11673149|lt=Lower Kōya Kaidō}}) extends narrowly into Matsubara City while remaining part of Osaka City <ref name = "Higashisumiyoshi explanation" /><ref name = "DP2">{{Cite web|Japanese book| url = http://portal.nifty.com/kiji/150312192969_2.htm | title = The Mystery of Osaka City’s Extremely Narrow Territory and the Kofun Curve 2 | date = 2015-03-13 | author = Akira Ōyama | publisher = Daily Portal Z | accessdate = 2015-09-13}}</ref>.

Until the early Meiji period, a {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} with the mountain name “Amamiyama” stood within the precincts, preserving a history of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}; however, it was abolished during the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|Q702298|qid=Q702298}} movement. The temple’s gate nonetheless remains along the approach <ref name = "Matsubara City explanation" />.

== Shrine buildings ==

يىلى|uk|1960|ur|1960ء|uz|1960|vec|1960|vi|1960|vls|1960|vo|1960|wa|1960|war|1960|wuu|1960年|xmf|1960|yi|1960|za|1960 nienz|zea|1960|zh|1960年|zh_classical|一九六〇年|zh_min_nan|1960 nî|zh_yue|1960年|qid=Q3754}} (Shōwa 35) <ref name = "Higashisumiyoshi explanation" />. Within the grounds are a gigantic {{ill|Camphora officinarum|Q158722|qid=Q158722}} over 500 years old and a statue of a sacred horse.

== Other ==
The place name Amami in {{ill|Matsubara|Q774952|qid=Q774952}} derives from Amami. Although the shrine lies within Osaka City, it serves as the tutelary shrine of the Amami area of Matsubara City <ref name = "Matsubara City explanation" />. On the other hand, as mentioned above, there are also descriptions identifying it as the tutelary shrine of Yata Village <ref name = "Higashisumiyoshi explanation" />.

Together with {{ill|Nunose Shrine|ja|布忍神社|qid=Q11480799}}, {{ill|Shibagaki Shrine|ja|柴籬神社|qid=Q11534936}}, Gadō Hachiman Shrine, {{ill|Miyake Shrine (Matsubara)|ja|屯倉神社|qid=Q11465762}}, and {{ill|Ao Shrine (Matsubara)|ja|阿保神社|qid=Q122900553}}, the six shrines conduct the “Kaiun Matsubara Six Shrines Pilgrimage” <ref>[https://matsubara-kanko.net/enjoy/rokusya/ Kaiun Matsubara Six Shrines Pilgrimage] Matsubara City Tourism Association</ref>. The five shrines other than Amamikoso Shrine are located within Matsubara City.

== Access ==
* Get off at {{ill|Minami Osaka Line|eo|Linio Kintetsu-Minami-Ōsaka|fr|Ligne Kintetsu Minami Osaka|it|Linea Kintetsu Minami-Ōsaka|ja|近鉄南大阪線|ko|긴테쓰 미나미오사카선|nl|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka-lijn|zh|南大阪線|qid=Q901342}} {{ill|Kawachi-Amami Station|arz|محطة كاواكى امامى|eo|Stacio Kawachi-Amami|it|Stazione di Kawachi-Amami|ja|河内天美駅|ko|가와치아마미역|my|ခဝချိ - အမမိဘူတာ|ur|کاواچی امامی اسٹیشن|zh|河內天美站|qid=Q6379447}}; about a 20-minute walk
* From {{ill|Osaka Metro (company)|wuu|大阪市高速电气轨道|zh_yue|大阪市高速電氣軌道|qid=Q51211653}} (Osaka Metro) {{ill|Midōsuji Line|Q1192413|qid=Q1192413|lt=Midosuji Line}} {{ill|Abiko Station (Osaka)|eo|Stacio Abiko (Osaka)|fr|Abiko (métro d'Osaka)|it|Abiko (metropolitana di Osaka)|ja|我孫子駅 (大阪府)|ko|아비코역 (오사카부)|nl|Station Abiko|ur|ابیکو اسٹیشن (اوساکا)|zh|我孙子站 (大阪府)|qid=Q2084534|lt=Abiko Station}}, take the {{ill|Hokkoh Kanko Bus|ja|北港観光バス|qid=Q11403750}} (bound for Amami Kita 2-chōme) and get off at Amami Shrine-mae
